definition: A triangular diagram with ionic, covalent and metallic bonding at its corners, on which a substance is placed using the average electronegativity and the electronegativity difference of its elements, so its position shows how much each type of bonding contributes.

A mixture of a metal with one or more other metals or non-metals, held together by metallic bonding; it has no fixed composition, so it is not a compound, and it is usually harder and stronger than the pure metal.
